title.narrative: EngenderHealth SRHR (Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights) Burkina Faso
EngenderHealth SRHR (Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter) Burkina Faso

description.narrative: EngenderHealth, project aims to expand access to quality abortion care and reduce unintended pregnancies among vulnerable populations and in humanitarian settings in Burkina Faso.

EngenderHealth, projektet syftar till att öka tillgången till kvalitativ abortvård och minska antalet oavsiktliga graviditeter bland utsatta befolkningsgrupper och i humanitära situationer i Burkina Faso.

The project aims to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality associated with unsafe abortion and increase the ability of women, including adolescent girls and young women, particularly those who are internally displaced and living in host communities, to realize their bodily autonomy. This will be done through four mutually reinforcing objectives: 1.Create a sustainable advocacy environment and a strong movement for quality safe abortion and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) 2.Improve the policy, legal, and strategic environment to advance quality abortion care 3.Increase the agency of women and adolescents to prevent unintended pregnancies and access quality abortion care 4.Improve availability of quality, integrated comprehensive abortion care (CAC), family planning (FP), and gender-based violence (GBV) services for underserved and displaced populations

Key results as per each of the four objectives of the 3M project include:
Objective 1: Create a sustainable advocacy environment and a strong movement for quality maternal and reproductive health care
- An analysis of the abortion ecosystem was carried out with an action plan supported by all stakeholders. The plan was validated by the Ministry of Health.
- The project regularly supported the Ministry of Health in its participation in international and regional meetings on sexual and reproductive health, particularly issues of access to abortion (for instance, at the African conference on SRHR and Family Welfare in Rabat, Morocco).
- Awareness-raising among health providers was carried out, reaching more than 300 providers. Moreover, values clarification sessions to question personally inherent norms and behaviours, were held where 130 participants, including judicial police officers and community leaders.
Objective 2: Improve the political, legal and strategic environment to advance quality care in maternal and reproductive health.
- The dissemination of the new abortion guidelines was carried out to health care providers, opinion leaders, decision-makers and power holders.
- A roadmap for access to safe termination of pregnancy with key actions included was developed and began implementation: review of the penal code to broaden the indications for abortion in Burkina Faso; revision of the provisions on third-party authorizations to access safe abortion under the law; revision of policies, standards and protocols to broaden the profile of providers of safe abortion; the plan for inclusion of Letrozole on the list of essential medicines (for breast cancer but can also be used as medical abortion drug in combination with misoprostol).
- A socio-anthropological study on the abortion situation in Burkina Faso, an analysis of gender, youth and social inclusion integration in the project and a client satisfaction survey on SRHR services offered at 32 health facilities were carried out with 165 clients surveyed, and a report validated by the Ministry of Health;
Objective 3: Increase the capacity of women and adolescents to prevent unwanted pregnancies and access quality post-abortion care and contraception.
- 8 networks of Choco Tanties, trusted aunts were set up with 24 tanties skilled in supporting, advising and guiding adolescents in schools and in their communities and producing menstrual hygiene sanitary commodities; community and safe space activities were carried out with referral systems established between health workers, safe space facilitators and the tanties as well as established collaboration between tanties, students and teachers, reaching 3,937 people. 1431 adolescents benefitted from SRHR counselling and support services.
- Between 2022-23 (year 1) and 2023-24, there was an 18% decrease in pregnancy cases in the project supported secondary schools in the five regions.
- 7 safe spaces were established in the 3 humanitarian regions in Centre Nord, Nord and Boucle du Mouhoun.
- A voucher system with 260 coupons for accessibility to services for girls, including in IDP camps, was put in place covering travel costs, contraceptive services and quality abortion care.
- 6717 women and girls were reached through awareness-raising on SRHR including access to safe abortion.
- Provision of psycho-social support and dignity kits to 450 vulnerable girls.
- 200 women received training in income-generation activities such as soap making, cotton loincloth weaving machines and tye-dying production.
- 30 radio programmes on SRHR were produced and broadcasted in local languages.
Objective 4: Improve the availability of quality integrated services in comprehensive abortion care, family planning and gender-based violence for underserved and displaced populations.
- 66 health facilities strengthened their capacities after a basic assessment which enabled them to be equipped with medical-technical equipment and to strengthen the skills of all service providers.
- The Quality-of-Care Framework was revised to consider abortion care;
- The humanitarian component has enabled the distribution of dignity kits to internally displaced women and girls and the training of village midwives in areas under blockade by armed terrorist groups in hygienic deliveries; 20 rural birth attendants received skills and safe delivery, misoprostol and medical protection kits in villages under military blockade.
- In 2024, 682 women had access to safe abortion care, exceeding the targets set for 2025, and 252 health providers were trained, 40% more than the initial target.
As for unexpected results, the intervention produced unintended positive effects, including increased awareness about sexual and reproductive rights in conservative contexts.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
